agentCan: Build the site-name + key connect form and the Basic Auth API plumbing

approval.cost: No fee for API keys or API access is stated in the docs read
approval.trigger: There is no app to review: no registration, submission, or approval step exists in the official docs. A connection works the moment a customer admin creates a key and hands it over. No developer listing or app-review process is described in the documentation read (Chargebee's docs reference a first-party Marketplace of built-in integrations under Apps > Go to Marketplace, e.g. QuickBooks, but no third-party submission/listing procedure is documented in the pages read). The operative constraint is not a user cap but shared rate quotas per site: a third party's volume counts against the merchant's 'overall API rate quotas'.

blockers.detail: There is no OAuth app registration, no client_id/client_secret for the Chargebee API, no authorize endpoint, and no consent flow anywhere in Chargebee's official documentation. The official API reference states the sole authentication mechanism plainly: 'Chargebee uses HTTP Basic authentication for API calls. The username is your API key while the password is empty.' A shared key is a standing, site-wide credential bounded only by its key type; there is no way for a customer to grant narrower, resource-level access, and no consent screen to show them what they are granting. Accuracy warning: several third-party blogs claim Chargebee has dashboard 'OAuth Apps' issuing client IDs/secrets and an oauth/authorize endpoint; NONE of that appears in Chargebee's official documentation and it contradicts the official API reference, so treat those claims as fabricated.
blockers.howToClear: No OAuth clearance exists. Use a dedicated, named, least-privilege key per customer and follow Chargebee's secure-sharing guidance.
blockers.title: No delegation, no scopes, no consent (and beware fabricated third-party claims)

blockers.detail: A key 'can be disabled or deleted using the more options button on the card for the key. Disabling a key prevents any applications using it from making API calls to Chargebee... Deleting a key purges it forever. The same key is never created again.' Either action is performed by the customer in their dashboard; your product cannot revoke or rotate its own credential. Rotation is a coordinated cutover: 'first create the new API keys, update all the existing keys on your application with the new keys, and only then delete the old keys from Chargebee'. If a customer rotates or deletes without telling you, your integration breaks silently until they share the new key.
blockers.howToClear: Build key-health detection (failed auth alerts) and a documented rotation runbook with each customer.
blockers.title: Revocation and rotation are the customer's manual job

tested: Read-only verification: the authentication model and the absence of any OAuth program were checked against Chargebee's official API reference and product docs (no account used, nothing submitted). The only OAuth flows in Chargebee's own docs are ones where CHARGEBEE is the OAuth client (a merchant connecting their Google Workspace / Microsoft 365 mailbox for SMTP notifications; Chargebee's built-in QuickBooks Online integration), not a way for a third party to get delegated access to a Chargebee site.
unverified: Whether Chargebee operates any partner/integration program outside the documentation read (e.g. a partner portal for its built-in Marketplace listings); no submission process, criteria, or timeline is described in the official docs read.
Any numeric API rate quotas per site (the docs reference 'overall API rate quotas' without figures in the pages read).
API key expiry (none stated; keys appear to live until disabled/deleted, but the docs read do not say this explicitly).
Any cost associated with API access tiers (not stated in the docs read).

alternatives: Full-Access Key ('Allows full access to Chargebee data with configurable read, write, and update levels'; at least one full access key must be present for a site)
Publishable Key ('Allows API calls from web browsers, such as creating and checking out subscriptions'; a browser-facing key, not a server integration credential)
flavor.recommended: No OAuth flavor exists. The documented pattern: each customer creates a dedicated, named key for your service, a Read-Only Key if you only read data, otherwise a Full-Access Key with the least access levels that work
flavor.why: The credential object is a per-site API key created by the merchant inside their own Chargebee site. The 'app' in this model is just a named key: Chargebee's best-practices doc advises using 'different keys for different apps', since 'Any given key acts as an identifier for the service that uses it' and the key's name appears as the user attribute on events the key triggers. Every site is a separate tenant with base URL https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2, so the connection is site name + key. Chargebee's own docs explicitly contemplate third-party key sharing: 'When sharing keys with a third party for integrations, ask about their API request volumes so that your overall API rate quotas are not breached.'

humanMust: The customer's Chargebee admin creates the dedicated key (Settings > Configure Chargebee > API Keys and Events > API keys > Add API Key); only users with admin access can view/create keys
The customer shares the key AND their site name through a secure medium ('Do not share keys via emails or other plaintext communication')
The customer performs any disable/delete/rotation in their own dashboard
name: Chargebee
nuances: Per-site sprawl: every customer is a distinct Chargebee site (subdomain) with its own keys, and 'The API keys are different for your test site and your live site', so your connect UX must collect site name + key for each environment separately.

Compromise blast radius: use one key per app so 'when a key is compromised, you only have to change it for the affected app'; 'Avoid using full access keys when publishable or read-only keys are sufficient'.

Auditability quirk: only POST-triggered events expose which key acted (event.user = key name); 'GET requests do not generate any events', so read activity by a shared key is not attributable in events.
Chargebee's stated rotation recommendation: 'Rotate API keys periodically... We recommend changing keys at least once in 3 months.' Keys have no stated expiry.
'At least one full access key must be present for a site; you cannot delete all of them.' Chargebee also warns merchants to 'Keep a tab on the number of people who have admin access' to the site.
prerequisites: A connect form collecting site name + API key, and secure credential storage
Per-environment key handling (test site and live site keys differ)

steps.detail: Settings > Configure Chargebee > API Keys and Events > API keys > + Add API Key: choose the type (Publishable / Full-Access / Read-Only), name it for your service, Create Key.
steps.title: Customer admin creates a dedicated, named API key

steps.detail: Per Chargebee's guidance, use 'a medium that is secure, has appropriate access restrictions, and is destroyed after key sharing' (e.g. a password manager). Your connect form needs both values because every site has its own base URL.
steps.title: Customer shares the key and site name securely

steps.detail: HTTP Basic auth with the API key as username and an EMPTY password (base64 of 'api_key:'), against https://{site}.chargebee.com/api/v2. Never commit keys to source control.
steps.title: Store the key; call the API with Basic auth

steps.detail: Test and live sites have different keys; repeat the handoff per environment and per customer. Plan the rotation cutover (create new key, update your app, then the customer deletes the old key) at least once every 3 months per Chargebee's recommendation.
steps.title: Repeat per environment; plan rotation

tagline: Chargebee has no OAuth program for third-party apps at all: the official API reference documents HTTP Basic auth with a per-site API key as the sole mechanism, and third-party blogs claiming Chargebee 'OAuth Apps' exist contradict the official docs. Connecting a customer means a named, least-privilege key handoff.
